Theme

Latin word

oportet

oportet, oportēre, oportuit

verb, second conjugation, impersonal, with an infinitive or an accusative and infinitive

it is right, one should; what is expected; one must, it is right; it is right, one should

In this lexicon

  • be supposed to

    the recommended word · classical · Plaut. Cas. 765–766: cēnam jam esse coctam oportuit; Ter. Heaut. 536: haec facta ab illō oportēbat

  • must

    also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 94.47: et discās oportet

  • should

    the recommended word · classical · Cato Agr. 3.1: aedificāre diū cōgitāre oportet; Phaedr. 4.18.9: parce gaudēre oportet

Examples

  • quīn agitis hodiē? quīn datis, sī quid datis? properāte, cēnam jam esse coctam oportuit.

    Come on, get moving! Hand it over, if you’re handing anything! Hurry: dinner was supposed to be ready by now.Plaut. Cas. 765–766

    In the entry for be supposed to

  • Haec facta ab illō oportēbat, Syre.

    That is what he ought to have done, Syrus.Ter. Heaut. 536

    In the entry for be supposed to
